stem: A transplant program is preparing an OPTN waiting-time modification application under Policy 3.7.A. Which required element must be included in the submission?

options.text: The name and signature of the candidate's physician or surgeon
Only the candidate's personal social media history
A guarantee of organ offer within 30 days
Proof that the candidate has never been listed before

explanation.rationale_correct: Waiting-time modification applications must include the requested listing date with documentation, evidence the candidate qualified under organ-specific OPTN policies, a corrective action plan if due to error, and the physician or surgeon name and signature.

rationale_incorrect.B: Applications require clinical and listing documentation rather than social media history.
rationale_incorrect.C: OPTN modification applications do not guarantee organ offers within a fixed interval.
rationale_incorrect.D: Prior listing history is addressed through documentation of requested listing date and qualification, not a blanket never-listed requirement.

primary_anchor.section: Policy 3.7.A → Applications for Modifications of Waiting Time → items 1.–5.
primary_anchor.quote_hint: The name and signature of the candidate's physician or surgeon

references.locator: Policy 3.7.A → Applications for Modifications of Waiting Time (physician/surgeon name and signature among required elements); PDF p. 50 (repo file-page index; printed margin may differ).

notes: Source-first item. First OPTN Policy 3.7 waiting-time modification item; distinct from inactive waiting-time Table 3-3 items (cctc-2037–2081); anchor verified on optn-policies p. 50.

stem: When coordinating preoperative education about organ procurement and implantation, which definition of cold ischemia time aligns with standard transplant immunology references?

options.text: The duration the organ is outside the body while preserved on ice
The time required to complete surgical revascularization in the recipient
The interval between two routine clinic visits after discharge
The total lifetime of the donor organ before procurement

explanation.rationale_correct: Cold ischemia time is the duration the organ is outside the human body during preservation on ice; warm ischemia time is the interval required to complete surgical revascularization in the recipient.

rationale_incorrect.B: Surgical revascularization time in the recipient defines warm ischemia time rather than cold ischemia time.
rationale_incorrect.C: Clinic follow-up intervals are unrelated to procurement ischemia definitions.
rationale_incorrect.D: Cold ischemia time measures preservation after procurement, not the donor organ's entire lifespan.

primary_anchor.quote_hint: time duration during which the organ is outside the human body is referred to as the cold ischemia time, whereas the time required to complete the surgical revascularization … is the warm ischemia time

references.locator: Ch. 2 → Ischemia-Reperfusion Injury (cold ischemia versus warm ischemia definitions); PDF p. 62 (repo file-page index; printed margin may differ).

notes: Source-first item. Cold-versus-warm ischemia definition angle distinct from delayed-graft-function supportive care (cctc-3088); anchor verified on Danovitch p. 62.

stem: During evaluation counseling for a pediatric lung transplant candidate, the team discusses parainfluenza virus (PIV) risk. Which statement aligns with standard infection references?

options.text: Viral shedding may be prolonged beyond 4 weeks in transplant recipients on long-term steroid therapy
PIV shedding always resolves within 24 hours in every immunosuppressed child
PIV infections are never more severe in children
PIV is relevant only to kidney transplantation

explanation.rationale_correct: In healthy individuals PIV shedding lasts about 1 week, but in transplant recipients—particularly those on long-term steroid therapy—shedding may be prolonged beyond 4 weeks; higher incidences occur in lung transplant recipients and more severe PIV infections occur in children.

rationale_incorrect.B: Immunosuppressed transplant recipients may shed PIV for prolonged periods rather than uniformly clearing within 24 hours.
rationale_incorrect.C: More severe PIV infections in children have been noted in transplant populations.
rationale_incorrect.D: PIV is described among community respiratory viruses affecting solid-organ recipients, with particular lung-transplant relevance.

primary_anchor.quote_hint: shedding may be prolonged (>4 weeks) … Higher incidences in lung transplant recipients and more severe PIV infections in children

references.citation: Core Curriculum for Transplant Nurses, 2nd ed. (Cupples et al., 2016).
references.locator: Ch. 5 → Parainfluenza viruses → 8.b.–c. (prolonged shedding on steroids; lung and pediatric severity); PDF p. 210 (repo file-page index; printed margin may differ).

notes: Source-first item. Eighteenth pediatric recipient in bank; parainfluenza evaluation-counseling angle distinct from lung bronchiolitis CMV (cctc-3073) and pulmonary rehabilitation (cctc-2034); anchor verified on Cupples p. 210.

stem: A patient is newly referred for cardiac transplantation evaluation. Which catheterization requirement aligns with standard heart evaluation references?

options.text: Both right and left heart catheterization
No cardiac catheterization because echocardiography replaces all invasive testing
Left heart catheterization only, with right heart studies permanently omitted
Catheterization only after transplantation, never during evaluation

explanation.rationale_correct: Patients referred for cardiac transplantation require both right and left heart catheterization as part of evaluation of cardiac function and anatomy.

rationale_incorrect.B: Cardiac catheterization remains part of cardiac transplant evaluation rather than being fully replaced by noninvasive imaging alone.
rationale_incorrect.C: Both right and left heart catheterization are required at referral rather than left heart studies alone.
rationale_incorrect.D: Catheterization is performed during pretransplant evaluation to assess candidacy and alternative procedures.

primary_anchor.section: Ch. 1, Evaluation → Heart transplantation → 4.a. Cardiac catheterization
primary_anchor.quote_hint: Patients referred for cardiac transplantation will require both a right and left heart catheterization

references.citation: Core Curriculum for Transplant Nurses, 2nd ed. (Cupples et al., 2016).
references.locator: Ch. 1 → Heart transplantation → 4.a. Cardiac catheterization (both right and left heart catheterization required); PDF p. 34 (repo file-page index; printed margin may differ).

notes: Source-first item. Initial cardiac cath requirement angle distinct from waitlist right-heart pressure monitoring (cctc-2057) and coronary angiography symptom reassessment (Cupples p. 35); anchor verified on Cupples p. 34.
